concept.title: Languages
concept.shortdesc: Publishing in Welsh or Spanish: the text the plugin adds to your pages follows the language of your content, and how to add another language.

conbody.p: languagesWelshSpanishYour content is in whatever language you write it in. Around it the plugin adds text of its own: the skip link, Contents, Search, the phase banner, the labels on warnings, figures and tables, the names of months in dates, and the buttons on the accordion home page. That text is in English, Welsh or Spanish, chosen by the xml:lang of your map and topics. There is no build parameter.

Where GOV.UK has published its own Welsh or Spanish wording for a piece of this text, such as the skip link, the accordion's buttons and the Open Government Licence line, the plugin uses it unchanged. The rest is the project's own translation.

section.title: Choosing the language
section.p: Set xml:lang on the map and on every topic:

table.title: Languages the plugin's own text is in

row.entry: en, en-GB, en-US, and any language not listed here

section.p: The map's language decides the home page, the search, glossary and index pages, and the order the glossary and index are sorted in. A topic's own language decides the text on its page, so a publication can hold topics in more than one language.

ul.li: The GOV.UK Design System is used as released. Its accordion script writes Show all sections and similar text; the plugin gives it the translated text through the attributes the Design System provides for that, and changes nothing in the script.
The search box and its results are written by Pagefind, which has translations of its own and chooses one from the page's language.
The GOV.UK and NHS names on the logos are not translated.
Glossary and index entries are grouped under the letters A to Z; a term that begins with an accented letter is grouped with the entries that begin with no letter.
Text is laid out left to right. A right-to-left language is marked as such on the page, but the layout is not mirrored.

section.title: Adding a language
section.p: The text lives in the plugin's strings folder, one file for each language. To add one, copy strings-en-gb.xml to a file named for the language, translate each value (taking GOV.UK's wording where it has one for the language), and add a line for each xml:lang value to strings.xml. Where the DITA Open Toolkit has no strings for the language, as with Welsh, add its labels too (strings-cy.xml shows which). Then install the plugin again.
Translations are welcome as contributions to the project.
